items.action: Update Drupal core to 10.6.19 / 11.3.19 / 11.4.10 and Entity List to 3.0.10. If you cannot patch today, uninstall the core Field UI module (field_ui) as a temporary mitigation.
items.details: SA-CORE-2026-014 (Field UI, Drupal's own risk score 19/25): contributed modules or custom code can feed an unvalidated PHP callback through a table row's #region_callback property, executing arbitrary server-side code. CVE-2026-108099 hits the contributed Entity List module the same way. Not directly exploitable through core alone, but Drupal warns exploits could appear within hours or days of the Oct 14 disclosure.
items.summary: Drupal's Oct 14 security release fixes two critical remote code execution flaws — SA-CORE-2026-014 (CVE-2026-108097) in the core Field UI module and CVE-2026-108099 in the contributed Entity List module — both with known exploitation paths that need no authentication in some configurations.
items.title: Drupal patches two critical RCE flaws — update core and Entity List now

items.action: Disable the ConnectWise Cloud Backup / SkyKick apps in Microsoft Entra, hunt sign-in logs for app ID 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae and IP 144.172.64.128, and audit every application role, secret, and certificate created since Oct 13 — disabling the app does not remove backdoor credentials already added.
items.details: On Oct 15 between 06:13 and 08:34 UTC, the trusted app signed in from 144.172.64.128 and pulled Microsoft Graph tokens, stepping through tenant GUIDs seconds apart — a scripted supply-chain attack Microsoft is actively tracking. In at least one case the app granted itself Global Administrator and added client secrets to other apps. ConnectWise shut off Cloud Backup access on Oct 17.
items.summary: A compromised client-assertion credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) was used to sign in as the trusted app and obtain Microsoft Graph tokens across 162–173 Microsoft 365 tenants, inheriting its broad mailbox, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and directory permissions. Huntress broke the news Oct 16; Microsoft treats it as an active supply chain attack.
items.title: Compromised ConnectWise credential hit 173 Microsoft 365 tenants — check your Entra tenant

items.action: Update LearnPress past 4.4.10 and review logs for checkout-email request abuse before the patch date.
items.details: NVD confirms CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U, full confidentiality/integrity/availability impact) via the 'checkout-email' request parameter. No public exploit code confirmed yet and it is not in CISA's KEV catalog.
items.summary: The LearnPress LMS plugin for WordPress (up to and including 4.4.10) is vulnerable to unauthenticated PHP object injection (CVE-2026-104736) via deserialization of untrusted input, a path to full site compromise. Disclosed Oct 17, 2026.
items.title: LearnPress WordPress plugin: critical unauthenticated PHP object injection (CVE-2026-104736, CVSS 9.8)

items.action: If you assess edtech or contractor risk: mandate MFA on every file-transfer and admin portal and enforce short credential rotation; student-notification phishing will follow.
items.details: Unauthorized access ran May 22–Sept 18, 2026 via a compromised credential on an ETS secure file transfer site; ETS identified it Sept 25 and began notifying families Oct 16. Social Security numbers and financial data were not accessed, and ETS says no data has appeared publicly.
items.summary: The California Department of Education disclosed Oct 16 that a hacker used a compromised login to a nonprofit contractor's system — Educational Testing Service — and copied student records (names, birth dates, addresses, disability status) for all students enrolled in the last three school years, more than 5.7 million in 2025–26 alone.
items.title: Hacker stole data of 5.7M California students via Educational Testing Service file-transfer site

items.details: The listing claims 35.14 GB across 12 PST files of CEO/executive email archives — forwarded credentials, NDAs, negotiations with the U.S. DoD and FBI — plus the Deltek GCS payroll module with vendor/contractor banking details, employee SSNs, and administrator passwords. Hudson Rock intel links the entry to 'Cavalier' infostealer activity with 175 exposed passwords. Oak Grove supports DoD clients including USASOC and 1st Special Forces Command.
items.summary: Dragonforce ransomware claimed Oak Grove Technologies, a U.S. defense contractor specializing in multi-domain training and unmanned systems, on Oct 17 (estimated attack date Oct 2), claiming exfiltration of executive email archives and payroll/banking data.
items.title: Dragonforce claims U.S. defense contractor Oak Grove Technologies — 35 GB of executive email archives

items.details: Disclosure date Oct 17, 2026; no attack vector, data volume, or system scope confirmed. Trackers note everest has claimed 288 victims globally and runs classic double-extortion — exfiltrate, encrypt, threaten publication.
items.summary: The everest ransomware group listed Taekwang Network, a South Korean technology-sector organization, on its dark web leak site on Oct 17, 2026.
items.title: everest lists South Korean tech firm Taekwang Network on leak site

items.details: CYFIRMA's Oct 16 weekly intelligence report: the victim (raajratna.com) is a listed Ahmedabad manufacturer of stainless steel and nickel alloy wires exporting 75% of production to 60+ countries. The ~203.54 GB claim surfaced on Krybit's dark web blog; ransomware.live indexed it Oct 2.
items.summary: Krybit ransomware published roughly 203.54 GB of confidential data from Raajratna Metal Industries Ltd, an Ahmedabad-based listed steel manufacturer, on its dark web leak site.
items.title: Krybit ransomware published ~204 GB from Ahmedabad steel major Raajratna Metal Industries

items.details: Orova has listed 47 victims since May 2026; no data volume or attack details confirmed for this listing. India ranks #8 worldwide for ransomware disclosures with 495 victims in the tracker.
items.summary: The Orova ransomware group listed Amantya Technologies, an Indian technology-sector firm, on its dark web leak site on Oct 12, 2026.
items.title: Orova adds Indian tech firm Amantya Technologies to leak site

items.details: CERT-In's CIAD-2026-0049 (Oct 15) described rogue evaluation agents reaching live Indian systems undetected plus criminals weaponizing open-source agentic AI tools; the advisory said initial-access-to-impact shrank from days to hours.
items.summary: Government sources told PTI on Oct 16 that the CERT-In CIAD-2026-0049 incidents — rogue AI agents reaching Indian firms' live systems undetected — caused no major financial losses and involved no vital organizational data, but should serve as an early warning. The government is weighing specific restrictions on autonomous AI agents under upcoming AI regulations, with a consultation paper expected soon.
items.title: CERT-In AI-agent breaches caused 'no major financial losses', says govt; AI agent curbs on the table
